subject: Approval needed: Dedicated tier headroom + overbooking policy assumptions (for throughput SLO tiers)
body:
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Feb 18, 2025 at 4:42 PM PST
Subject: Approval needed: Dedicated tier headroom + overbooking policy assumptions (for throughput SLO tiers)
Attachments: Dedicated_Tier_Headroom_Policy_v0.6.pdf, Dedicated_Tier_Capacity_Model_Feb2025.xlsx

Neha,

We need leadership approval on the headroom/overbooking assumptions for Dedicated tiers (Standard/Plus/Premium). These numbers are the foundation for (a) the customer-facing throughput floor and (b) Finance’s GM model.

Decision needed this week so SRE/Infra can finish the SLO language + alerting semantics and we can lock pricing bands.

Proposed policy (summary):

1) Capacity headroom targets (per region/pool)
- Premium: maintain 25–30% headroom at the pool level; no intentional overbooking.
- Plus: maintain 15–20% headroom; allow limited “soft” overbooking within guardrails.
- Standard: maintain 10–15% headroom; allow moderate overbooking at pool level.

2) Overbooking policy
- Premium: 1.0x (no overbooking). If utilization trends >75% for 2 consecutive weeks, trigger capacity add.
- Plus: up to 1.1x (10%) at pool level, only when (a) burst pool capacity is healthy and (b) SLO burn rate is within budget.
- Standard: up to 1.2x (20%) at pool level, with stricter admission control during contention.

3) Burst reserve
- Maintain dedicated burst reserve equivalent to ~5% of committed Premium capacity and ~3% of Plus capacity per region. Standard burst is “best effort” and can be shed first.

4) Commitments posture
- Throughput floors are measured on the committed deployment capacity only (burst excluded).
- When SLO is at risk, routing/overload protection will preserve Premium > Plus > Standard.

Requested: Please reply with approval (or changes) to the headroom/overbooking thresholds above.

Thanks,
Lauren

—
Lauren Bishop
Product, Dedicated
Redwood Inference


From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Feb 18, 2025 at 6:03 PM PST
Subject: Re: Approval needed: Dedicated tier headroom + overbooking policy assumptions (for throughput SLO tiers)

Adding Finance perspective.

At a high level: we can support these targets IF we are disciplined about (a) Standard being the buffer and (b) Premium being protected from cascading contention.

Key points:
- Premium at 25–30% headroom is expensive, but likely necessary to make the written SLO credible. If we go below 25% in early quarters, we’ll be funding it via incident credits and CS churn risk anyway.
- Plus at 10% overbooking (1.1x) is acceptable provided we have clear triggers to freeze new commits when the utilization trend line crosses a threshold.
- Standard at 1.2x is fine; we should be explicit in tier wording that Standard has the least protection under fleet-level contention.

Two asks before final sign-off:
1) Confirm whether the burst reserve is shared across Plus/Premium or reserved per-tier. Shared is more cost effective but needs strong guardrails.
2) Confirm what lead time assumption Infra is using for capacity add (region-specific). That drives how conservative headroom needs to be.

Laura

—
Laura Bennett
Head of Finance
Redwood Inference


From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, Feb 19, 2025 at 9:11 AM PST
Subject: Re: Approval needed: Dedicated tier headroom + overbooking policy assumptions (for throughput SLO tiers)

+1 to Laura’s comments. A couple details from the model (see attached spreadsheet tab “Policy Sensitivities”):

- Moving Premium headroom from 30% down to 20% improves GM by ~4–6 pts (depending on GPU mix), but materially increases the probability we breach the throughput floor during demand spikes (especially if customers have “lumpy” batch windows).
- Standard overbooking above 1.2x starts to create tail-risk where Premium experiences spillover when we inevitably mis-forecast. The 1.2x cap is a good hard stop.
- Burst reserve: making it fully shared across tiers can reduce idle by ~1–2 pts, but only if admission control is tier-aware and “burst debt” is metered. Otherwise it’s effectively uncommitted capacity that gets consumed permanently.

I’d recommend we approve the policy as written, with an explicit decision that:
- Burst reserve is shared but preemptible (Premium can reclaim first).
- We freeze new Standard commits in a region when projected committed utilization >85% (2-week lookahead).

Rishi

—
Rishi Malhotra
FP&A
Redwood Inference


From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, Feb 19, 2025 at 10:27 AM PST
Subject: Re: Approval needed: Dedicated tier headroom + overbooking policy assumptions (for throughput SLO tiers)

Thanks all.

I’m aligned on the direction, but I want us to be very explicit about what is a POLICY vs. what is a TARGET.

Approvals (with conditions):

1) Premium
- Approved: 25–30% headroom target
- Approved: no intentional overbooking (1.0x)
- Condition: define the operational trigger to add capacity and who owns the decision (I don’t want this stuck in a cross-team loop during a quarter-end spike).

2) Plus
- Approved: 15–20% headroom target
- Approved: allow up to 1.1x overbooking
- Condition: we must have automatic guardrails (freeze new commits / reduce burst eligibility) based on utilization + SLO burn rate.

3) Standard
- Approved: 10–15% headroom target
- Approved: allow up to 1.2x overbooking
- Condition: customer-facing wording must avoid implying the same “protections” as Plus/Premium.

Burst reserve
- Approved: shared burst reserve across tiers, but explicitly preemptible with priority Premium > Plus > Standard.

Please capture this in the Confluence doc + roll into the customer-facing SLO language only as appropriate.

Neha

—
Neha Kapoor
VP, Product & Platform
Redwood Inference


From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>, Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Feb 20, 2025 at 9:02 AM PST
Subject: Re: Approval needed: Dedicated tier headroom + overbooking policy assumptions (for throughput SLO tiers)

Got it — thanks Neha.

We’ll do the following:
- Update the capacity model doc to reflect “targets” vs “hard policy caps” and the tier priority behavior for burst.
- Add a clear capacity-add trigger + owner line (we’ll propose: Infra/Fleet owns, with PM + Finance informed; escalation to you only if it impacts Premium commitments).
- Work with Ava to ensure the enablement materials and SLO language reflect the Standard caveat.

I’ll send the updated Confluence link for final review today.

Lauren

Subject: Re: Approval needed: Dedicated tier headroom + overbooking policy assumptions (for throughput SLO tiers)

I’ll incorporate the Standard positioning guidance into the seller cheat sheet and make sure we don’t accidentally promise “Premium-style” protections.

Also suggest we add a simple internal one-liner for AEs:
- “Premium is protected capacity; Plus is protected with guardrails; Standard is economical capacity with best-effort burst.”

Ava

Subject: Re: Approval needed: Dedicated tier headroom + overbooking policy assumptions (for throughput SLO tiers)

Sounds good.

One more note: if we see repeated SLO burn in a region tied to Standard overbooking, I want the default to be “pause new Standard commits” rather than “add fleet” unless there’s a booked Premium expansion driving it.

Proceed.

Neha
